claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 17 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 17 and in the 20-week extension period
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**What is the age of the child (or children) you're inquiring about?**

To help me guide you through the eligibility check, please tell me:
1. How many children do you have that you're asking about?
2. What are their ages?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son, Alex. He's 17 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, your 17-year-old son** who lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's education or training status. 

**Is Alex currently in education or training?** 

For example:
- Is he at school or college?
- Is he on an apprenticeship or other training scheme?
- Or has he recently left education/training?

Please let me know his current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He recently left education actually. He finished school not too long ago and has been working with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. So Alex has recently left education and is currently working with the careers service.

Let me check whether he qualifies for an extension to Child Benefit eligibility based on the timing and circumstances of leaving education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is an important check. There's a **20-week extension** available for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left approved education or training.

**To qualify for this extension, I need to confirm:**

1. **How long ago did Alex leave school?** (We need to know if it was within the last 20 weeks)
2. **Has he registered with any of these services?**
   - Government careers service (like the one he's working with)
   - Connexions
   - Armed services

Can you confirm these details for me?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's registered with the careers service - that's who he's been working with to figure out his next steps. And it's been within the last 20 weeks since he left school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex meets the requirements for the 20-week extension:
- ✓ He's registered with the careers service
- ✓ He left school within the last 20 weeks

Now let me check the next requirement for eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is an important requirement - if he's working 24 hours or more per week (while not in approved education/training), this would affect his eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now. He's just been focusing on working with the careers service to figure out what direction he wants to go.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex is not in paid work at all, which means he meets this requirement.

Let me check the next eligibility criterion.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any certain benefits in his own right.

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

In other words, is he receiving these benefits in his own name/right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He doesn't get Universal Credit or ESA or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good! Alex doesn't receive those benefits in his own name. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is in an apprenticeship. There are regional rules that apply here:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

If yes, please let me know:
- What type of apprenticeship? (e.g., Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, Degree Apprenticeship, Modern Apprenticeship, Foundation Apprenticeship, etc.)
- Which country is he based in? (England, Scotland, or Wales)

If he's not in an apprenticeship at all, just let me know that.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. As I mentioned, he's just been working with the careers service since leaving school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you (the claimant) normally live in the UK?**

Or, if you don't normally live in the UK, do you have one of these circumstances:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with specific conditions like working, studying, jobseeking, or having sufficient resources)?
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries?

Please let me know your residency situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You meet the residency requirement. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. 

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
- You live with him (which you've already confirmed), OR
- You contribute to his upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.), OR
- You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you've already said you live with Alex at home, you clearly meet this requirement. Let me proceed.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example:
- Is his other parent claiming?
- Is a grandparent or other relative claiming?
- Or are you the only person claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation.

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- Is he in hospital?
- Is he in care (like a children's home)?
- Is he fostered?
- Or is he living normally at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me. Nothing unusual about his living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is the final eligibility check. 

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, the council is not providing financial support for his housing or upkeep, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. He just lives here with me as a normal family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex meets all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit. Let me provide you with the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

---

### **Summary of Your Situation:**

You have successfully met all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for your 17-year-old son, Alex. Here's why he qualifies:

**Key Eligibility Factors:**
- ✓ Alex is 17 years old (16-19 age group)
- ✓ He recently left school **within the last 20 weeks**
- ✓ He is **registered with the government careers service** (which qualifies him for the 20-week extension)
- ✓ He is **not working full-time** (in fact, not working at all)
- ✓ He is **not receiving disqualifying benefits** (no ESA or Universal Credit in his own name)
- ✓ He is **not in a disqualifying apprenticeship**
- ✓ You **normally live in the UK** (residency requirement met)
- ✓ You **live with Alex** and are responsible for him
- ✓ **No other person is claiming** Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ Alex is **living normally at home** with you
- ✓ The **local council is not paying** for his accommodation or maintenance

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year
5. Payments are made **every 4 weeks** (or weekly depending on your circumstances)

---

### **Important Note:**

The 20-week extension will end at:
- Week 20 from when Alex left school, **OR**
- When Alex turns 18, **whichever comes sooner**

After the extension period ends, Alex will need to be in approved education or training to continue receiving Child Benefit until age 19.

For more information and to apply, visit: **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**

Congratulations! You should be able to start receiving Child Benefit for Alex shortly after your application is processed.

There are no other claimants for Alex, and the local council is not providing financial support."
